# Executive should grant an action point and a single hand slot

The Executive staff card (`staff-executive`) should be repurposed from a pure hand-capacity card into an action-economy card: while employed it grants **+1 action per week** and **+1 hand slot**. This extends the `actionsPerTurn` staff mechanic (introduced by MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0) to the tier-10 Executive and reduces its `handSlotsAdded` from `4` to `1`.

## Problem statement

The Executive is the tier-10 premium capacity card (`handSlotsAdded: 4`, cost 2000, ongoing 500) with no ability. Players who want a top-tier action-economy staff choice currently have only the tier-12 General Manager, so the Executive is a dead-end on the action-economy build axis. Granting the Executive `actionsPerTurn: 1` — traded against dropping its hand-slot bonus to a single slot — gives it a distinct, legible role.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a tier-10 action-economy staff option before the tier-12 General Manager is affordable.
- **Main Street player (mid/late game)** — wants the Executive's role to be clear: a tempo (extra action) card rather than a bulk hand-capacity card.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want to hire an Executive that grants +1 action per week and +1 hand slot so that I can take an extra action each week without waiting for the General Manager.
- As a Main Street player, I want the Executive's card art, tooltip and description to state the +1 action/week and the single hand slot so that I understand what I am buying.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `src/card-data.csv` `staff-executive` row sets `actionsPerTurn` to `1` and `handSlotsAdded` to `1` (down from `4`), keeping `cost: 2000`, `ongoingCost: 500`, tier `10`, and the generalist `allowedBusinessTypes` (`Food|Culture|Service|Commerce|Entertainment|Health`); the CSV `description` states the `+1` hand slot and the `+1` action/week (and no longer claims "major hand capacity" / `+4` slots). CSV column order is unchanged.
- **AC2** — The parsed `StaffCard` template for `staff-executive` exposes `actionsPerTurn === 1` and `handSlotsAdded === 1`, and `executeWeekStart` composes the weekly budget as `1 base + sum(actionsPerTurn) + banked (capped at 2)` with the Executive included, preserving the existing invariants (staff actions consumed first, never banked; bank cap 2).
- **AC3** — The staff card formatting and Actions HUD tooltip render the Executive's `Actions: +1/week` benefit and the in-game Help panel "Turn Flow" text lists the Executive among action-granting staff (Manager, Director, Executive, General Manager).
- **AC4** — The committed card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` is regenerated to show `+1 slots` (not `+4 slots`), and `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` matches the new `src/card-data.csv` content.
- **AC5** — Tests assert the new Executive contract and no-regression for staff without the ability: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (Executive grants +1 action/turn and +1 slot; only Manager, Director, Executive and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (the Executive design-contract entry and the non-ability block are updated so the Executive is no longer listed as ability-free), and existing action-budget/tooltip tests remain green.
- **AC6** — Documentation is updated to reflect the change: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ 6.0 action-economy staff list), `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (staff table), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (staff catalogue row + rationale), and `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` (staff template table).
- **AC7** — All related documentation and user-facing text (code comments/doc-strings, `README.md` where it references the affected card or the action list, in-game help panel) is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mechanic already exists** — reuse `actionsPerTurn` (CSV column, `StaffCard.actionsPerTurn`, `executeWeekStart`, tooltip/formatting). No new engine mechanic, schema column, or save-format change is expected; the change is data + card art + docs + test coverage.
- Preserve the existing action-economy invariants: bank cap of 2, base-only banking, staff actions consumed first and never banked, and the defensive clamp in `executeWeekStart`.
- CSV column order must remain unchanged (edit in place); `actionsPerTurn` is already a known column.
- Do not alter the Manager, Director or General Manager as part of this item.
- Card SVG generation is driven by the CSV + `csv-checksum.json`; the committed SVG must be regenerated with the project generator (`node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) rather than hand-edited.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: `staff-executive` = `handSlotsAdded 4`, no `actionsPerTurn`, `cost 2000`, `ongoingCost 500`, tier 10, description "An experienced executive adds major hand capacity at a high ongoing cost."
- Action-granting staff today (MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0): Manager (tier 3, 700/250, +1 slot, +1 action), Director (tier 9, 1400/400, +3 slots, +1 action), General Manager (tier 12, 2000/500, +4 slots, +1 action). The Executive, Apprentice, Socialite, Accountant, Lookout, Investor and the specialization applicants do not grant actions.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` (`executeWeekStart`): budget = `1 + sum(staff.actionsPerTurn ?? 0) + min(2, bankedActions)` — logic is already generic.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (staff case): renders `Actions: +N/week` when `actionsPerTurn > 0`; `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` (`buildActionTooltip`) appends the generic action-granting-staff note when any employed staff has `actionsPerTurn > 0`.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` "Turn Flow" body lists "(Manager, Director, General Manager)".
- Card art `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` currently renders `+4 slots`; `csv-checksum.json` is committed alongside.
- Tests today: `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` (asserts the ladder and "only Manager, Director and General Manager grant `actionsPerTurn`"), `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (Executive contract `handSlotsAdded: 4`; Executive in the "staff without the ability" block), `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/staff-business-type-matching.test.ts` (Executive generalist — should remain unchanged).

## Desired change

- CSV: `staff-executive` → `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, description updated to state the `+1` hand slot and `+1` action/week.
- Card art: regenerate `staff-executive.svg` and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Help/tooltip text: add the Executive to the "Turn Flow" action-granting-staff list (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`); confirm `MainStreetFormatting`/`MainStreetHudTooltips` need no logic change.
- Docs: update the four tables/sections listed in AC6 and the action-economy staff list.
- Tests: assert the Executive's new contract and update the "only these staff grant actions" and "staff without the ability" assertions; add a week-start budget composition case including the Executive.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — `staff-executive` row: `actionsPerTurn 1`, `handSlotsAdded 1`, refreshed `description`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/staff-executive.svg` — regenerated card art showing `+1 slots`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum matching the new CSV.
- `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` — Executive contract + broaden the action-granting set; add composition case.
- `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — update the Executive design-contract entry and remove it from the "no ability" block.
- `tests/main-street/hud-tooltips.test.ts` — cover the Executive-derived action budget where relevant.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — assert the Executive appears in the action-granting-staff list.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — add the Executive to the "Turn Flow" staff list.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — refresh the `actionsPerTurn` doc comment if it names only the General Manager.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — verify `executeWeekStart` composes the budget with the Executive included; no logic change expected (AC2).
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — verify the existing `Actions: +N/week` rendering needs no logic change (AC3).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — verify the generic action-granting-staff tooltip note needs no logic change (AC3).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — § 6.0 action-economy staff list.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row and rationale.
- `docs/main-street/prd-multi-use-card-economy.md` — staff template table.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance dominance (assumption / open question):** with `handSlotsAdded: 1` + `actionsPerTurn: 1` at `2000/500` tier 10, the Executive is strictly dominated by the Director (tier 9, `1400/400`, `+3` slots, `+1` action) and by the General Manager (tier 12, `2000/500`, `+4` slots, `+1` action). **Assumption:** the operator intends the literal `+1` slot / `+1` action, and tier-gating (Executive unlocks before the General Manager) is the intended differentiator; any cost/tier rebalance is out of scope for this item. See the Appendix open question.
- **Scope-creep risk:** regenerating SVGs touches only the Executive's card content, but the checksum file changes for the whole CSV; treat that as a generated artefact — do not hand-edit other SVGs.
- **Assumption:** the `actionsPerTurn` engine path is already generic (verified in `executeWeekStart`), so no engine change is required; if a hidden General-Manager-specific assumption surfaces, prefer generalising the comment/text over special-casing.
- **Failure mode:** forgetting to regenerate `csv-checksum.json` would make the runtime regenerate art on load and could break checksum tests — regenerate both together.
- Out of scope: any change to the Manager, Director, General Manager, the bank cap, or the save format; any new card or art beyond regenerating the Executive SVG.

## Related work

- **MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0 — Some staff cards should add action points** (completed): introduced `actionsPerTurn` on the Manager and Director and documented the ladder Assistant → Manager → Director → Executive (+4 slots). This item supersedes that item's AC2 statement that the Executive stays at `+4` slots.
- **MS-0MTISBYLS009936W — Add Investor staff members** (completed): precedent for adding a staff ability (`freeMarketRerollPerTurn`) via CSV + types + docs + tests.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** (Group F staff expansion epic) and **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY**: introduced the Executive as a premium capacity card.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R**: original General Manager action-economy mechanic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The Executive will become `+1` hand slot and `+1` action/week at 2000/500 tier 10. That makes it strictly dominated by the Director (tier 9, 1400/400, +3 slots, +1 action) and the General Manager (tier 12, 2000/500, +4 slots, +1 action). Should the Executive's cost/ongoing/tier also be adjusted, or should the literal `+1` slot / `+1` action be implemented as written and any rebalance handled separately?" — **OPEN QUESTION.** No operator answer recorded during intake. **Agent recommendation (advisory):** implement the literal request now (AC1–AC8) and raise a separate balance work item if the dominance is confirmed as unintended; alternatively reduce the Executive's `cost`/`ongoingCost` (or raise its slots) so it is not strictly worse than the Director.
  - Evidence: `src/card-data.csv` staff rows; `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` staff table; `tests/main-street/action-economy.test.ts` ("only Manager, Director and General Manager grant actionsPerTurn").
- Q: "Does 'a single hand slot' mean `handSlotsAdded` should be `1` (replacing the current `4`)?" — Answer (derived from the work-item description and title, not an interactive reply): yes — the description explicitly says "grant an action point and a single hand slot", and this brief assumes the current `+4` is reduced to `+1`. Source: `wl show MS-0MUYAEXBN008YC0J`.
- Q: "Is a duplicate of an existing item?" — **Duplicate check performed** (`wl search executive|action economy|staff balance|hand slot`): closest match is MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0 (completed), which intentionally left the Executive unchanged. This item is a **partial overlap / extension**, not a duplicate; the brief addresses only the Executive delta. Source: `wl search` results; `wl show MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUMM69OL008ZMK2** – Commit game-repo scaffolding files (.githooks, AGENTS.md, package-lock.json) (open)
- **MS-0MUOSUMNK000QZ62** – Update documentation for Investor card and mechanics (completed)
- **MS-0MV33NV6O002WBYA** – Test: per-seat challenge completion attribution (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, actions (+318 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: abilities, ability, acceptance, action, actions (+250 more)
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — matched: 0msqj7vl9009jhf4, 0mstof1n5005pk2r, 0mtisbyls009936w, 0mtq7s5ej008mwd0, ability (+245 more)

# Piggyback on other players' organiser actions

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) play, when one player organises a town-wide event such as a Local Festival, the benefits are currently routed only to that acting player's own wallet (`applyCompetitiveEventEffects`). There is no way for the other player(s) to participate in, or benefit from, an event that thematically belongs to the whole town. This makes events feel private rather than communal and removes a legible, interesting per-event decision from the non-acting player.

## Users

Primary user: the **human player in competitive mode**, who wants a meaningful reactive decision when the AI organises a town event.

- As the human player, when the AI organises a festival, I want to choose whether to co-fund it so that I can earn the full reward, or simply enjoy the spill-over benefit for free.
- As the human player, I want the trade-off to be explicit (coins and action cost vs. reward share) so the decision is legible.
- Secondary user: the **AI seat**, which needs a deterministic policy for the same decision so headless Monte Carlo runs stay reproducible.

## Proposed mechanic (design summary)

When a player plays a **piggyback-eligible Investment event** (an "organiser" event — e.g. Local Festival, Harvest Festival) during their MarketPhase, every **other active player** receives a 50% share of that event's rewards **automatically**, and is offered the single choice to **join fully**:

| Option | Cost | Reward |
|--------|------|--------|
| **Join fully** | **150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event** (paid from the piggybacker's own coins); **no action point is spent** | **100%** of the event's rewards |
| **Free-ride (automatic default)** | Nothing | **50%** of the event's rewards, granted automatically |

- The free-ride 50% is always applied, so there is **no "decline everything" option** and no prompt to refuse it — the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade 50% → 100%.
- Joining fully does **not** consume an action point; the seed's "take an additional action" means the player participates in the event (an additional participant), not that a budget action is spent.
- Rewards (coin + reputation) are computed on the **piggybacker's own board**, consistent with the existing per-owner event routing (`SpecificSynergy` rewards count the owner's own matching businesses), then scaled to 100% (join fully) or 50% (free-ride).
- The cost baseline is the amount the acting player **actually paid** for the event (after any cost discounts the acting player holds), not necessarily the card's nominal listed cost.
- If the piggybacker cannot afford 150% of that cost, the join-fully option is unavailable and the 50% free-ride applies.
- The acting player's own reward, and the shared market/incident deck, are unaffected by piggyback decisions.
- The mechanic applies **only in competitive mode (N≥2)**; single-player (N=1) has no other players and is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Eligibility & trigger.** When an active player plays a piggyback-eligible **organiser** Investment event during their MarketPhase in competitive mode (N≥2), every other non-eliminated player automatically receives the 50% free-ride share and is offered the join-fully upgrade for that event; playing a non-eligible event (or any event in N=1) produces no share and no prompt. Verified by unit tests over a flagged eligible card and an unflagged card.
- [ ] **AC2 — Join-fully tier.** Choosing "join fully" deducts exactly 150% of the cost the acting player paid for the event from the piggybacker's own coin balance (and **no action point**), then credits the piggybacker 100% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board). The option is unavailable (and never partially charged) when the piggybacker cannot afford the cost. Verified by unit tests asserting exact before/after coin and reputation values and an unchanged action budget.
- [ ] **AC3 — Free-ride tier.** Every non-acting eligible player automatically receives 50% of the event's rewards (computed on their own board) with no prompt to decline, spending no action point and no coins. This is also the fallback when "join fully" is unaffordable. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Isolation, determinism & persistence.** The acting player's reward and all shared decks are byte-for-byte unchanged by piggyback decisions; decisions for N>2 are resolved independently per seat in a deterministic order with no additional RNG draws; a pending piggyback decision survives a save/load round-trip. Verified by tests (including a replay/equality check and a serialize→deserialize→resolve test).
- [ ] **AC5 — AI policy and human prompt.** AI seats decide whether to join fully via a deterministic strategy heuristic in `MainStreetAiStrategy`; the human seat is offered the choice to join fully (pay the cost for 100%) or keep the automatic 50% free-ride, through the existing choice/prompt plumbing. Verified by an AI-policy unit test and a scene/command-layer test for the human prompt.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md`, and any relevant PRD/scope notes.
- [ ] **AC7 — Tests.** New unit tests cover eligibility, both tiers, the unaffordable fallback, N>2 isolation, AI policy and save/load; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Presentation and economy scale.** Costs in this game are large (Local Festival lists at 300 coins; Harvest Festival and similar events are comparable). 150% of a 300-coin event is 450 — a significant sink — so the AI heuristic and the human prompt must state the exact coin cost and the resulting reward share.
- **Determinism.** Competitive mode is exercised by a headless Monte Carlo harness and deterministic replay/transcript tests; the mechanic must not introduce additional RNG draws in the resolution path.
- **Per-owner authority.** `PlayerRecord.coins` / `.reputation` are authoritative in competitive mode (the shared `resourceBank` is a scratch mirror). Piggyback cost and reward must mutate the piggybacker's `PlayerRecord`, not the shared wallet.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Adding a per-card eligibility flag must default to "not eligible" so existing card data and save files are unaffected; older saves without the pending-piggyback field must load with a null default.
- **Turn terminology.** Use canonical "turn"/"week" vocabulary; player-facing text is guarded by `scripts/check-terminology-guards.sh`.

## Existing state

- Competitive mode (N players on one owner-tagged street, alternating MarketPhases within a shared day) is implemented engine-side. `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` orchestrates the shared day; `endCompetitiveMarketTurn` round-robins seats.
- Investment events are played during the acting seat's MarketPhase via `playEventFromHand` (`MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`) and dispatchers in `MainStreetEngineActions.ts` (`buy-event`, `play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`).
- `applyCompetitiveEventEffects` (`MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`) already routes an Investment event's deltas to the **acting player only** (`actingId`), and computes `SpecificSynergy` rewards per owner from that owner's matching businesses. This is the natural seam for a scaled (100%/50%) piggyback reward.
- Per-card data lives in `src/card-data.csv` with an extensive column set; event rows currently carry `trigger`, `effect`, `target`, `targetSynergy`, `coinDelta`, `reputationDelta`, `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId`, etc. There is **no** piggyback/eligibility column yet.
- A precedent for deferring a player decision already exists: dual-choice incidents stash `state.pendingEventChoice` and pause the turn with `TurnResult.choicePending`, then resolve via `resolveEventChoice` / `resolveEventOption`; the pending choice is serialized in `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The piggyback decision should reuse this "pending decision + pause/resume" pattern.
- AI action enumeration and scoring live in `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`; there is no piggyback decision yet, and no repo occurrence of "piggyback" anywhere.
- Actions are budgeted per seat (`PlayerRecord.actionBudget`) and partly bankable (`state.bankedActions`, capped at 2). Piggybacking does **not** spend an action point; the acting player's normal action consumption is unchanged.

## Desired change

- Add a per-card **piggyback-eligibility** flag (CSV column + `EventCard` field) defaulting to false, and mark organiser events such as Local Festival / Harvest Festival as eligible.
- When an eligible event is played in competitive mode, raise a **pending piggyback decision** for each other active player; pause/resume the shared day using the existing pending-choice pattern so the acting player's resolution completes first.
- Apply the chosen tier: join fully = −150% of the cost the acting player paid, +100% rewards (no action cost); free-ride = +50% rewards, applied automatically. Rewards are computed from the piggybacker's own board via the existing per-owner event math (then scaled).
- Add a deterministic **AI join-fully policy** and a **human prompt** offering join-fully vs. keep-50% (no decline option).
- Serialize/deserialize the pending decision; keep older saves loading.
- Update docs, code comments and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `piggybackable` column; mark organiser event rows (Local Festival, Harvest Festival, …) as eligible.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` / `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — parse and expose the eligibility flag on `EventCard`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `playEventFromHand` / `playHeldEvent` hook that raises piggyback opportunities after the acting player's event resolves.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — reward computation seam: scale and route event rewards to a piggybacker's own wallet.
- `src/MainStreetEngineActions.ts` — cover both event-play dispatch paths (`play-event`, `play-event-from-hand`); new piggyback `PlayerAction` variants if needed.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — pending-piggyback state machine, pause/resume of the shared day.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` / `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — pending-piggyback state shape and action/result types.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` / `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — persist the pending decision with a null default for older saves.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — deterministic AI piggyback decision policy.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (+ overlay/HUD renderers) — human prompt for the decision.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/main-street/ai-strategy.md` — document the mechanic, tiers and AI policy.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — competitive-only scope.** The mechanic applies only when N≥2; single-player has no other player to piggyback on. Revisit only if a solo "friendly town" flavour is later wanted.
- **Confirmed — free-ride is automatic.** Per the producer, the 50% free-ride is always applied and never offered as a decline option; the only player decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%.
- **Confirmed — no action-point cost.** Joining fully spends coins only (150% of the acting player's paid cost); the action budget is untouched.
- **Risk — economy runaway.** Stacking 100%-reward participation across many organiser events could inflate a seat's economy. Mitigation: the 150% cost premium; re-run the competitive Monte Carlo harness and record before/after win-rate/score attribution.
- **Risk — turn-resume complexity.** Pausing the shared day to await a piggyback decision touches the same deferred-closing machinery as dual-choice incidents. Mitigation: reuse the `pendingEventChoice` pattern and cover pause/resume + save/load with dedicated tests (AC4/AC5).
- **Risk — AI legality.** The AI must never attempt the full tier without the action or coins. Mitigation: share one affordability predicate between the eligibility gate and the AI policy, tested directly.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Extending piggybacking to business purchases/upgrades/staff hires is out of scope unless Q1 selects option (c); record any such desire as a separate linked work item rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- `MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ` — *Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution* (feature, completed) — establishes the per-owner event routing this mechanic builds on.
- `MS-0MT5X3GMA007EG30` — *Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street* (epic, done) — the competitive engine this mechanic extends.
- `MS-0MTSHG8RP008E128` — dual-choice incident deferred-resolution pattern (referenced in code comments; the save/load and pause/resume precedent to reuse).
- `MS-0MUVUPWHD0032CU4` — *Turns do not bank when playing against AI* (completed) — action-budget/banking rules a piggyback action must respect.
- `MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2` — *AI seat elimination with business closure* (completed) — defines "other active players" (non-eliminated seats only).
- `MS-0MUR9IN7L0004TO5` — *Re-price community spaces and events…* (completed) — the event cost/reward baseline used by the 150%/100%/50% maths.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed intent was clear on the headline rule but left several design details open. All questions below were answered by the producer on 2026-10-07; the confirmed answers are recorded inline and the brief has been updated to match.

- **Q1 — Which actions are piggyback-eligible?** — Answer (producer): **organiser events only** (option a) — a per-card opt-in flag on Investment "organiser" events (festivals, fairs, community gatherings); not all Investment events and not purchases/upgrades/staff hires. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2 — What does "take an additional action" mean, and is the 50% tier a choice?** — Answer (producer): joining fully **does not cost an action point**; it costs **150% of the cost paid by the original (acting) player**. There is no point in declining the 50% free-ride, so **no decline option is offered** — the 50% share is automatic and the only decision is whether to pay to upgrade to 100%. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3 — Reward and cost baseline for the piggybacker.** — Answer (producer): **confirm** — rewards are the event's deltas computed on the **piggybacker's own board** (per-owner `SpecificSynergy` matching), scaled ×1.0 (join fully) / ×0.5 (free-ride); the cost is 150% of the cost the acting player paid (per Q2). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q4 — Multi-player prompt ordering and simultaneous decisions.** — Answer (producer): **as recommended** — decisions are solicited and resolved one seat at a time in seat order, independently per seat, before the shared day continues. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

data.description:
# Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes

## Problem statement

A storyline choice node currently declares exactly **two** labelled outcomes
— "Accept" (yes) and "Reject" (no), each pointing at one successor card
(`hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` in `src/card-data.csv`).
Authors cannot express richer branches, and a chosen outcome always leads to
the same next card. The goal is to let a node present an **arbitrary number
of labelled outcomes**, where each outcome holds a **set of candidate
successor cards** and the actually-visited successor is selected **uniformly
at random** when the player picks that outcome. Producer direction
(2026-10-14, interactive reply): Q1=B (arbitrary labelled player options,
engine picks the successor from an option's candidate set at random);
Q2=A (extend CSV authoring + author CLI + validator + graph/manifest/schema,
**no backward compatibility** required, mermaid documentation must be
re-worked); Q3=A (uniform selection via the seeded `state.rng()`, one draw
per selection at resolution time so replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic).

## Users

- **Content/engine authors** — need to declare multi-outcome nodes with
  random branch targets from CSV without programmatic registration.
- **Players** — see an arbitrary labelled option list instead of a forced
  Accept/Reject; repeat plays of the same storyline can take different
  successor paths.
- **Balance team** — benefit from Monte-Carlo determinism being preserved
  (same seed ⇒ same branch), so the existing harness remains comparable.

Example user stories:

- As a content author, I can declare a node with three outcomes
  ("Negotiate", "Walk away", "Escalate"), each listing two possible next
  cards, so a single choice can fan into varied consequences.
- As a player, when I pick an outcome the game resolves to a uniformly
  random one of that outcome's candidate successors, without me choosing the
  next card.
- As a balance engineer, I can re-run a seeded simulation and observe the
  same random branch taken, so storylines remain auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Arbitrary labelled outcomes.** A storyline choice node can declare an arbitrary number (≥ 1, including > 2) of labelled options authored via CSV (`src/card-data.csv`), each option carrying its own ordered candidate list of successor card ids (empty list = the chain ends).
- **Uniform random selection.** When an option is chosen, exactly one successor is drawn uniformly at random from that option's candidate set using the seeded `state.rng()` (one draw per selection, at resolution time); replaying with the same seed produces the same successor, and the option list the player sees is unchanged by the draw.
- **Legacy shape removed.** The two-way `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/ `rejectNextCardId` fields and their compiled Accept/Reject semantics are replaced by the arbitrary-outcome model (no backward compatibility kept); the five shipped storylines are migrated, with the timeline of the change documented in the work item.
- **Tooling consistency.** The authoring CLI, static validator (`validate-storylines.ts`), graph/manifest export and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` all model the new option/successor-set shape, rejecting dangling targets, empty option lists and malformed option encodings.
- **Documentation regeneration.** Mermaid graphs, per-storyline documents (`docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`), the storyline reference (`docs/main-street/storylines.md`) and any doc-drift tests/SVG artefacts are regenerated to show the new multi-outcome nodes and pass their drift guards.
- **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover compilation, resolution (random draw semantics incl. a seeded replay pair), validator and CLI authoring; the storyline regression harness plus the full project test suite pass with the new changes.
- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
## Constraints

- Determinism: successor selection may consume RNG only from the seeded
  `state.rng()` stream, exactly one draw per selection; `pushChainCard`
  stays RNG-free. Any additional draw shifts the stream and must be pinned
  by tests, so cross-build Monte-Carlo comparisons after this change are not
  numerically identical to before (acceptable — see Risks).
- No backward compatibility: legacy fields, compiled Accept/Reject shape and
  `'accept'`/`'reject'` transcript/save tokens may be removed; per producer
  decision (Q5) no old-save handling is implemented — no saves exist in the
  wild — so legacy load paths are dropped cleanly.
- The generalised `StorylineOption` seam (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`)
  remains the single compilation/resolution point; the AI and UI paths flow
  through it unchanged in structure.
- CSV authoring must keep the deterministic, machine-parseable, validator-
  gated style of the existing tooling.

## Existing state

- Choice data lives on `EventCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) and is
  authored in `src/card-data.csv` via `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`
  (Accept/"yes", effect `apply`) and `rejectNextCardId` (Reject/"no",
  effect `skip`); legacy fields compile to a two-option `StorylineOption`
  list in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`.
- A programmatic registry (`registerStorylineOptions`) already supports
  arbitrary labelled options with `condition` / `successorResolver`
  callbacks; content authoring via CSV has never used it.
- Resolution: `resolveIncident` defers the choice into
  `pendingEventChoice`; `resolveEventOption`/`resolveEventChoice` apply the
  effect policy and push the single successor (`pushChainCard`, no RNG).
  `decideEventChoice` picks an option index on the AI path; transcript
  records `'accept'`/`'reject'` tokens (`MainStreetTranscript.ts`); saves
  store the `chosenOption` token (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`).
- The shipped graph has five storylines; the manifest, Mermaid flowchart,
  per-storyline SVG docs and the schema are regenerated via
  `npm run storylines:graph…` and covered by drift guards and
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- Extend the CSV data model so a row can author an arbitrary labelled option
  list, each option with an ordered candidate successor set. Suggested
  encoding (decided in planning, kept deterministic; Q4=B): a single
  `options` column of the form `label|cardA,cardB;label2|cardC` (option
  separator `;`, label/successors separator `|`, candidate separator `,`),
  replacing the three legacy columns; `hasChoices` derives from a non-empty
  list; every CSV-authored option carries `effectPolicy: 'apply'` (`skip`
  remains available only via the programmatic registry seam).
- Change the compiled model: `StorylineOption` gains a candidate successor
  list (`successorIds: string[] | null`) in place of the single
  `successorId`; `resolveStorylineOption` draws one uniform candidate via
  `state.rng()` at resolution time, applies the option's `effectPolicy`
  (always `apply` for CSV-authored options per Q4=B), and pushes the drawn
  card. `successorResolver` (if present) keeps precedence
  over the random draw, and `condition` keeps draw-time filtering with the
  frozen snapshot.
- Migrate the five shipped storylines to the new model, update the
  validator, author CLI (`storyline-author.ts`), graph/manifest export,
  JSON schema, transcript/save/undo tokens, AI decision handling and UI
  option presentation as needed, and regenerate all graph/SVG/doc artefacts.
- Record follow-ups (not in scope): weighted outcomes, per-candidate
  conditions, UI redesign of the option dialog. See Related work.

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — replace `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` with the arbitrary `options` column; migrate five storylines.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` choice fields; `StorylineOption.successorId` → candidate successor list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — compilation of CSV options, uniform draw via `state.rng()`, resolution precedence (resolver > random > none).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution path, transcript token, `resolveEventChoice` indexing.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — validate arbitrary option model (labels, successor sets, dangling targets, empty lists).
- `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — author CLI for multi-outcome nodes.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph*.ts` — edges per option → each candidate successor; Mermaid/SVG re-render.
- `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` — node options + edge model.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — option-label tokens, save/undo.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI option pick over arbitrary lists (static chain eval re-worked).
- `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` — option label presentation.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`, graph artefacts in `docs/main-street/assets/` — regenerate; drift guards.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/storyline-*.test.ts`, `storyline-regression-harness.test.ts`, `storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, `MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts`, `storyline-graph.test.ts`.

## Related work

- MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N (completed) — generalised `StorylineOption` seam & callback escape hatch; foundation for this change.
- MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9 (open, feature) — conditional/cost-gated options; design overlap, different semantics — keep separate, coordinate on the shared option model.
- MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7 (open, task) — Monte-Carlo storyline coverage analytics; benefits from deterministic random branches.
- MS-0MURO2D6F002WM4Y (blocked) — planned validator/schema extension for conditional fields; superseded/re-scoped by this change.
- MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV (completed) — "write storylines" epic; origin of the shipped content being migrated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'an arbitrary number of yes and no outcomes' mean?" — Answer (producer, 2026-10-14 interactive reply): **B** — the node presents N labelled player options (arbitrary labels); each option's successor is randomly drawn from its own candidate set. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up: "Change description to match this new direction" — description rewritten accordingly.
- Q2: "Where are the multiple outcomes authored and which surfaces change?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A** — extend CSV authoring + author CLI + validator + graph/manifest/schema; **no need to maintain backward compatibility**; "there will need to be work on the mermaid graphs in documentation". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "How should random selection behave under deterministic replay?" — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A** — uniform random using seeded `state.rng()`, one draw per selection at resolution time; replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic. Source: interactive reply.

## Risks & assumptions

- **RNG stream shift (accepted).** Adding a seeded draw at each resolution changes the shared RNG stream relative to the previous build; seeded replays *within* the new build are deterministic, but Monte-Carlo/balance numbers are not numerically comparable across the change. Mitigation: pin the draw count and stream position in tests; document in the work item.
- **CSV encoding of nested lists is error-prone.** Mitigation: strict validator with actionable errors; keep separators deterministic and documented in the CSV column reference.
- **Old saves (decided Q5).** No backward compatibility is required, and no old-save handling is implemented — there are no saves in the wild; legacy load paths are dropped cleanly (documented in child F3).
- **AI difficulty heuristics.** Hard-difficulty static chain evaluation is built around accept/reject chains and needs re-work for arbitrary options; AI must still resolve headlessly without stalling.
- **Scope creep.** Weighted outcomes, per-candidate conditions, and a redesigned option dialog are explicitly out of scope; record as follow-up work items (see Related work).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV16VXPV002JVX5** – Verification: pack unlock, purchase & save/load pipeline (completed)
- **MS-0MUVBH589001L7NL** – Competitive game ends on AI seat failure — reputation collapse or bankruptcy (eliminate AI instead of ending human game) (completed)
- **MS-0MV1HAUPR004REDJ** – [test-failure] main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts > suite import failure — failing test (completed)
